posts.topic: AI training reality check
posts.text:
Quick reality check on AI training gigs:

The legit ones (DataAnnotation, Outlier, Prolific, TELUS) do pay real people. But "accepted" and "working" are two different things. Outlier workers call it the empty queue.

If you're trying this, apply to 3 at once and keep your regular job search running alongside.

posts.topic: How to pass a one-shot AI training test
posts.caption:
Some AI training platforms give you ONE shot at the entry test. DataAnnotation's Starter Assessment can't be retaken, and if you don't pass you may never hear back.

Here's how to give yourself the best chance:
✅ Read every instruction twice
✅ Accuracy beats style, so check the math
✅ Justify with the exact sentence
✅ Never use AI to write your answers
✅ Block 90 quiet minutes

Save this for test day 📌

posts.topic: Assessment tip
posts.text:
The most common way people fail AI training entry tests isn't lack of knowledge.

It's missing an instruction. "Under 100 words." "Explain why." "Use bullet points."

Read the prompt twice before you write a single word.

posts.topic: AI interview tip
posts.text:
AI interviewers (Mercor, Alignerr's "Zara", micro1) build their questions from your resume.

So before you start: pick your 3 biggest projects and practice explaining each in 2 minutes. What you did, how, and the result with a number.

Vague resume = vague interview.

posts.topic: Upwork first-client timelines
posts.text:
What first-client timelines on Upwork actually look like, from freelancers on Upwork's own community forum:

• "About 2 months to land my first client, and 3 weeks after that to land my next"
• Others sent proposals for 6 months, and broke through only after narrowing their niche

If you're 3 weeks in with nothing, change the profile, not just the number of proposals.

Before you take a "work from home" call-center gig, check one thing: W-2 or 1099?

Some contractor models charge you up front. Liveops, for example, says agents pay a $25 background check, certification is unpaid, and some programs pay 25–34¢ per talk minute.

Do the math on your real hourly rate first.

posts.topic: ATS myth
posts.text:
Unpopular opinion: the "75% of resumes get auto-rejected by ATS" stat gets repeated way more than it's backed up.

Most ATS systems parse your resume and let recruiters search keywords. The real killers are tables, columns, and contact info stuck in the header.

Simple single-column resume > fancy template.

posts.topic: Rewrite your resume with AI in 45 minutes, honestly
posts.caption:
AI can tailor your resume in minutes, but only if you give it rules.

The 45-minute workflow:
1️⃣ Decode the job: must-haves + exact keywords
2️⃣ Fit check: score 1–10, skip below 6
3️⃣ Tailor with rules: "Use only my facts. Never invent numbers."
4️⃣ Test the PDF: copy-paste it into a text editor

Golden rule: if you can't explain a line in an interview, delete it.

Save this for your next application 📌
